items.title: Every rune has two jobs
items.body: A basic rune can be exhausted to add 1 energy, or recycled to add 1 power of its own domain. Exhausting comes back next turn; recycling sends the rune to the bottom of your Rune Deck, so you're trading future energy for power right now. Recycle only when the power wins you the turn.

items.title: Spend it or lose it
items.body: Energy and power sitting in your rune pool don't carry over — the pool empties between phases and at the end of the turn. Only exhaust or recycle runes when you're about to pay for something.

items.title: Going second? Plan a 3-energy turn one
items.body: In 1v1 the player going second channels one extra rune on their first turn. Keep a 3-cost play in your opening hand when you know you're on the draw.

items.title: Mulligan with a plan
items.body: You may set aside up to 2 of your opening 4 and draw that many; the set-aside cards go to the bottom of your deck, not back into the shuffle. Ship expensive cards first — a hand that can act on turns 1–3 wins more than one with a single bomb.

items.title: Hidden: big cards for 1 power
items.body: Any card with [Hidden] can be hidden facedown at a battlefield you control for 1 power of any domain. From your next turn it gains [Reaction] and you play it ignoring its base cost. A 4-energy Consult the Past (draw 2) becomes a 1-power instant draw on your opponent's turn.

items.title: Ava Achiever skips the hiding step
items.body: When Ava Achiever attacks you may pay 1 Mind power to play a [Hidden] card from your hand at that battlefield, ignoring its cost — no need to hide it a turn early. Load your hand with high-cost Hidden cards and attack with Ava.

items.title: Ember Monk loves Hidden
items.body: Ember Monk gets +2 might each time you play a card from [Hidden]. Hide cheap tricks for 1 power, then flip them during a fight Ember Monk is in to swing combat twice.

items.title: Brazen Buccaneer for 4
items.body: Brazen Buccaneer costs 6, but you may discard a card as you play it to reduce its cost by 2 energy. Pitch a card that's dead in the matchup (a late-game Catalyst, an extra copy of a situational spell).

items.title: Commander Ledros eats the board
items.body: As you play Commander Ledros you may kill any number of friendly units as an additional cost; each one reduces his cost by 1 Order power. Feed him units that have already done their job — especially ones with [Deathknell] so you get value twice.

items.title: Black Rose Dignitary pays for itself
items.body: Black Rose Dignitary has [Deathknell]: channel 1 rune exhausted when it dies. Sacrificing it to Commander Ledros reduces Ledros by an Order power and ramps you a rune at the same time.

items.title: Daisy! can cost almost nothing
items.body: Daisy! costs 9 but is reduced by 1 energy for each of the tags Bird, Cat, Dog and Poro among your units — and she enters ready. With all four tags she's 5 energy, attacks immediately, and stuns an enemy unit when she attacks.

items.title: Acceleration Gate refunds itself
items.body: Acceleration Gate readies up to 4 units, gear and/or runes. Ready 4 exhausted runes and you can exhaust them again for 4 energy — the 3-cost spell nets you energy and can also ready units for a second attack.

items.title: Catalyst of Aeons is never dead
items.body: Catalyst of Aeons channels 2 runes exhausted — and if you couldn't channel 2 (your Rune Deck ran low), it draws a card instead. Early it ramps, late it cycles.

items.title: Find Your Center gets cheaper when it matters
items.body: Find Your Center draws 1 and channels a rune, and costs 2 energy less once an opponent is within 3 points of winning. Hold it for the turn they get close: 1 energy for a card and a rune.

items.title: Fiora + Dragon Form: instant ramp
items.body: Fiora, Grand Duelist lets you exhaust her to channel a rune when one of your units becomes [Mighty] (5+ might). Dragon Form sets a unit's base Might to 5 — so it makes a unit Mighty on the spot, and you can recast it later from your trash with [Flow].

items.title: Arcane Shift: replay your best 'when you play me'
items.body: Arcane Shift banishes a friendly unit and its owner plays it again ignoring its cost — then deals 3 to an enemy unit at a battlefield. Use it on a unit whose value is in its play effect to get that effect a second time for free.

items.title: 'Ignoring its cost' still lets you pay extras
items.body: When you play something ignoring its cost, its base energy and power costs become 0 — but optional additional costs like [Accelerate] can still be paid, and must be paid in full if you choose them.

items.title: Order your discounts
items.body: When several discounts apply, component discounts (like Eager Apprentice's −1 energy, minimum 1) apply before whole-cost discounts. With Eager Apprentice out, Sky Splitter can drop all the way to 0 if you apply the Apprentice first — the rulebook uses this exact example.

items.title: Units enter exhausted
items.body: Units come into play exhausted, so they can't attack the turn you play them — unless something says otherwise. [Accelerate] (1 energy + 1 power of the card's domain) makes a unit enter ready; Bushwhack readies everything you play that turn.
items.src: Core rules (units enter the board exhausted), Accelerate

items.title: Bushwhack turns a big turn into lethal
items.body: Bushwhack makes friendly units enter ready this turn and gives you a Gold gear token. It has [Hidden], so you can hide it the turn before for 1 power and play it for 0 energy, leaving all your runes for the units you want to swing with.

items.title: Coalesced Energy: best early
items.body: At the end of your turn Coalesced Energy recycles all your runes, then channels 4 exhausted. With fewer than 4 runes out it's pure ramp; with more than 4 it shrinks you — play it early or when your runes are low.

items.title: Aphelios gets three bonuses a turn
items.body: Each time you attach Equipment to Aphelios, Exalted you pick a different mode that turn: ready 2 runes, channel 1 rune, or buff a unit. Two equips can mean ready 2 runes (to pay for the second equip) plus a free extra rune.

items.title: Baited Hook upgrades a unit
items.body: Baited Hook (1 energy + 1 Order, exhaust) kills a friendly unit, then lets you play a unit from your top 5 with up to 1 more Might, ignoring its cost. Sacrifice a spent 2-might unit to hit a 3-might threat for free.

items.title: Dazzling Aurora: a free unit every turn
items.body: Dazzling Aurora is expensive at 9, but at the end of each of your turns it reveals cards until a unit and plays it ignoring its cost. Run it in decks heavy on big units and it pays back in two turns.

items.title: Death from Below comes back
items.body: Death from Below kills a unit at a battlefield; if that unit had 3 might or less you may play it again from your trash for 1 power. Aim it at small threats first to get two kills from one card.

items.title: Flow cards are two cards in one
items.body: [Flow] lets you play a card again from your trash for its Flow cost, then banish it. Dredge Up draws 1 for 2 energy — and again later for 2 from the trash. Count Flow cards as card advantage when building.

items.title: Tank and Backline decide who dies
items.body: Combat damage must go to [Tank] units first and to [Backline] units last. Protect a key unit by pairing it with a Tank, or give your best attacker Backline so blockers can't pick it off.

items.title: Deflect taxes their removal
items.body: [Deflect] makes opponents pay a rune of any color to choose your unit with a spell or ability. Against removal-heavy decks, that extra rune often breaks their turn's math.

items.title: Recycling isn't shuffling
items.body: Recycled cards go to the bottom of their deck — main deck cards to the main deck, runes to the Rune Deck. [Predict] and [Vision] let you push a dead top card to the bottom so you draw something better next.

items.title: Temporary units die before you score
items.body: [Temporary] units are killed at the start of their controller's Beginning Phase, before scoring. Don't count on a Temporary unit to hold a battlefield for points next turn.

items.title: Drag Under is cheaper from anywhere but your hand
items.body: Drag Under (kill a unit at a battlefield) costs 2 energy less when played from anywhere other than your hand. Watch for effects that let you play cards from your trash or the top of your deck — that's a 3-energy kill.

items.title: Weaponmaster saves a rune
items.body: [Weaponmaster] units can equip one of your Equipment when played for a rune less — even moving it off another unit. Equipment-heavy decks should count Weaponmaster units as extra rune economy.
